title: Interdependence & competition
group: BIO-EVOL / BIO-ECOL / BIO-PLANT — Evolution, Ecology & Plants
examples: Can you explain what a biotic factor is in an ecosystem?
How does a predator-prey cycle keep a population stable?
What is the difference between competition and interdependence?

explain.say: Today we learn about how living things depend on each other. This is called interdependence in nature.
Next we look at the things around living things. These are the abiotic factors we study.
Biotic factors are the living parts of an ecosystem. These include plants and animals.
Predator-prey relationships show one animal eating another. The predator hunts for food always.
A real-life example is a forest food web. Deer eat plants, and wolves then eat the deer.
A common mistake is forgetting that abiotic factors affect life. For example, drought limits plant growth.

faq.q: What is the difference between biotic and abiotic factors?
faq.a: Biotic factors are the living or once-living parts of an environment. Abiotic factors are the non-living physical parts of that environment.
asks: What counts as non-living in ecology?

faq.q: How does competition work between species?
faq.a: Competition happens when two or more organisms need the same limited resource. This could be food or shelter for example.
asks: Do all species compete for resources?

faq.q: In a predator-prey cycle, what happens if the prey population increases greatly?
faq.a: If the prey increases, the predator population will likely increase next. This creates a cycle of boom and bust.
asks: Does the predator population follow the prey?
How does predator increase affect prey?

faq.q: Are all interactions in nature interdependence?
faq.a: No, not all interactions are interdependence. Some interactions are purely competitive, like two lions fighting over one kill.
asks: What is the opposite of interdependence?

faq.a: Yes, abiotic factors can create interdependence. For instance, the presence of a river (abiotic) supports fish and plants (biotic).
asks: Does water count as an abiotic factor?

facts: Interdependence means organisms rely on each other for survival.
Abiotic factors include sunlight, temperature, and water.
In predator-prey relationships, the predator consumes the prey.
Competition occurs when multiple species need the same limited resource.

quiz.say: A desert ecosystem has very little water. This lack of water is an example of:
quiz.why: Water is a non-living physical component of the environment.

wrong.1: This is wrong because biotic factors must be living things.
wrong.2: This is wrong because it describes an interaction, not a physical factor.
wrong.3: This is wrong because competition is an action between organisms.

quiz.say: A hawk hunting a rabbit shows which relationship?
quiz.why: The hawk is the predator and the rabbit is the prey in this interaction.

wrong.1: This is too general; predator-prey is a specific type of interaction.
wrong.2: This is wrong because only one animal is shown hunting another.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the hawk and rabbit are both living organisms.

quiz.say: When two types of grasses grow in the same field, they are competing for:
quiz.why: Competition involves multiple organisms needing the same limited resources like space or nutrients.

wrong.1: Predation involves one animal eating another, which is not happening here.
wrong.2: The grasses themselves are biotic, not the resource they share.
wrong.3: Interdependence implies mutual reliance, not just a struggle for resources.
